Attacker is the party named in entry point ("attacker-influenced text... influenced through injection or the user"). AV=L (local, relies on user opening report / local CLI). AC=L. AT=P? Requires specific condition: input makes model pass crafted body — that's somewhat beyond attacker's control? Injection or user influencing the model is probabilistic; AT=P reasonable. PR=N (unauthenticated). UI=A (person must open the report in browser). Impact: stored XSS in browser — subsequent system? The vulnerable system is the agent process; the browser/session of the person opening the report is a subsequent system. SI=H (script execution in victim's browser... but what site? It's a local file; JS runs in browser context, can access cookies? file:// — limited). I'd give VC=N, VI=L (attacker-controlled content written to a file — actually the agent writes it, VI=L), VA=N. SC=L, SI=H (arbitrary JS in the victim's browser), SA=N.

The entry point says "influenced through injection or the user" — attacker-supplied NL reaches tool path. LC=D (direct if user task text) or I (indirect via fetched pages). Ambiguous; entry point: title/body of write_report influenced through injection or user. The attack corpus includes fetched attacker-edited pages. I'll say LC=I (attacker-controlled language via retrieved content influences behavior)? But user could be the attacker directly. Since it says "injection or the user", injection via fetched web content → I. Actually "user" — the person who runs CLI writes the task. If the user is the attacker, that's D. Mixed; go with I since injected content via fetch_url is a main channel. Hmm. Direct: attacker-supplied NL reaches privileged tool-invocation path without mediation — if attacker is the CLI user, D. But user opening report is the victim (same person?). The briefing says "a person opens the generated report." The attacker is the party in entry point — injected content author. I'll pick I.

CP: context persistence — does the XSS persist across sessions? out/report.html is a file written; the attacker-controlled HTML persists on disk and executes later. CP=C is about agent memory stores. The report file is durable but not agent memory. CP = S? Session context? The payload persists as a file beyond the session, but that's a source-content artifact, not agent memory. Rubric: "Stored source content that is only re-retrieved... is not CP." I'd say CP=S or N. Attack happens in one run; the injected context lives within session; report persists but that's the impact, not memory. CP=S with testing? Not verified unreachable. I'll use X? Evidence: memory is persistent (S8), but this path doesn't use memory. CP=N: single-run path, no memory carryover needed. Go CP=N.

AP: contained — same principal? Affects the person opening the report, a different... it's within same machine/domain. AP=C (relays across components under same principal) or N (confined to write_report/report file)? Effect confined to the output file. AP=N.

RH: any evaluator/reward channel reachable? The path is write_report output; no evaluator. reachable_proxy=false not verified; verified_episodes unknown → X.

ES: extensions — tools are fixed built-ins, allowlisted (12 built-ins), but args unvalidated and MCP possible. On this path, write_report built-in. ES=M (allowlisted but gaps)? MCP attached only if caller passes one; default no MCP. Arguments not validated → M? "Managed: allowlisted, material gaps in argument schemas." Yes, ES=M.
